title: TS SDK: Stream Swapper — unified consumer pattern experiments
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Context: The TypeScript SDK needs a pragmatic pattern for callers that must switch between consumption models (async iterator vs. Web Streams ReadableStream) at runtime without losing progress, leaking memory, or breaking cancellation/retry semantics. Many integrations (serverless, browser, worker threads) prefer different primitives and sometimes need to hand off an in-flight stream when environment constraints change (e.g., move from Node worker to main thread, or switch to a browser-compatible ReadableStream).

Problem: Existing adapters provide conversion helpers but don't handle live consumer swaps, retries after transient network errors, or strict cancellation propagation consistently. Current issues observed in prototypes: partial token duplication after retry, lost backpressure signals, unclosed resources on consumer swap, and awkward ergonomics for developers to implement safe handoff.

Goal: Prototype and validate a "Stream Swapper" helper in the TS SDK that: 1) exposes both async-iterator and ReadableStream consumer views, 2) allows an explicit, safe handoff from one view to another mid-flight, 3) preserves cancellation semantics and retry idempotency, 4) keeps memory bounded under backpressure, and 5) is ergonomically simple in common use cases.

Scope: Build RFC + experiment code + integration tests + small demo app. Provide clear examples for SDK consumers and migration notes. Non-goals: rework server runtime scheduling, change wire protocol, or add new transport protocols beyond existing streaming endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamSwapper helper that can create both an AsyncIterator and a ReadableStream view of the same underlying response stream
Swapping from AsyncIterator to ReadableStream mid-stream transfers remaining tokens without duplication or loss
Cancellation requested from either view reliably closes the underlying connection and surfaces the cancellation to the other view (if swapped) as a thrown error
Retry logic (at the request layer) can redeliver safely when swap is not performed; when a swap is in-progress the helper provides a documented fallback behavior
Benchmarks show memory usage remains bounded for 99th percentile sequence lengths up to 8k tokens under backpressure
Comprehensive unit and integration tests, plus a small example app (browser + Node) demonstrating a mid-flight swap
tasks: Draft RFC for StreamSwapper API and trade-offs
Implement experimental StreamSwapper in ts-sdk/stream-swapper.ts in playground branch
Add adapter tests: asyncIterator -> swap -> ReadableStream and reverse
Add cancellation propagation tests and retry interaction tests
Run mem/latency bench on simulated load (bounded queue sizes) and document results
Write example demos: serverless function that starts iterator then hands off to browser ReadableStream via postMessage
Collect reviewer feedback and iterate on API ergonomics
Prepare a migration note for existing adapter users
decisions: Design will surface an explicit 'swap()' call rather than implicit automatic handoff to keep semantics deterministic
Underlying implementation uses a small bounded internal queue (configurable default 16 chunks) to smooth boundary between consumer models

Retry semantics: retry is allowed only before swap() is called. After swap(), caller must either accept potential duplication or opt into 'idempotent markers' API for server-side dedupe later. We will document this as a user-visible constraint rather than attempt complex server-side coordination in this iteration
Cancellation will propagate via a single CancellationController shared by both views; throwing CancellationError on the other view when appropriate
Keep adapter surface minimal: provide 'toAsyncIterator()', 'toReadableStream()', and 'swapToReadableStream()' helpers on the returned StreamSwapper
open_questions: Should swap() be synchronous (blocking until handoff completes) or return a promise? (current implementation returns Promise<void> to allow async draining)
Is a configurable queue size enough for production workloads, or do we need an adaptive backlog that grows/shrinks based on observed latencies?
How do we document and recommend behavior for consumers that rely on exact token offsets (e.g., eval harnesses) when swap + retry could cause duplication?
Do we want a higher-level convenience API that performs automatic retry/dedupe for simple cases? Cost/complexity tradeoff needs product input
comments: 2025-02-10 — Aisha N. Patel: Created ticket and initial design intent. Included prototype goals and acceptance criteria. Linked to prototype branch once created.

2025-02-12 — Miguel R. Santos: Implemented first-pass StreamSwapper in playground branch: github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/412 (WIP). Observed duplication when swapping after partial retry — investigating whether buffer re-sequencing is root cause.
2025-02-14 — Priya Kaur (PM): Reviewed RFC; suggested making swap() explicit and flagged UX concern for serverless-to-browser handoff. Wants a clear 'migration note' for existing adapter users.

2025-02-16 — Design review (Evan J.): Suggested example with postMessage Transferable stream for handing from worker to main thread; noted we should validate on Chrome/Firefox and Safari differences. Added a task for cross-browser demo.

2025-02-18 — Miguel R. Santos: Fixed a race where iterator consumer acknowledgement could sneak past when swap() concurrently drained the internal queue. New approach holds a swap lock until transfer completes. Added tests covering the race.

2025-02-20 — QA (Lena T.): Ran basic memory regression tests; peak RSS reduced with bounded queue from previous unbounded approach. Still need to validate under bursty inputs (next: 10k simulated requests).
2025-02-21 — Aisha N. Patel: Pushed updated RFC per feedback. Requested review from runtime team on retry semantics. Added dependency on ENG-4721 for stream contract details.
notes: Implementation sketch: core uses an AsyncGeneratorSink that writes into a RingBuffer. toReadableStream() uses a custom underlying source that pulls from the ring buffer; toAsyncIterator() yields directly from async generator. swapToReadableStream() marks the iterator as closed for consumer and transfers ownership of buffer read pointer to the readable source.

Testing: add fuzz tests that randomly swap consumers, inject transient network error, and assert no token duplication/loss. Also add cross-browser manual tests for ReadableStream transfer via postMessage in example app.
Metrics to collect: tokens-per-request distribution, queue occupancy percentiles, swap latency (time between swap() call and readable becoming available), memory RSS P50/P95 under synthetic loads.

Edge cases: final chunk emission after swap, partial chunk reassembly across boundaries, large single-chunk frames ( > queue size ) — ensure we fallback to passthrough mode for oversized frames and surface a warning to the user
